claims.gist: Most companies adopt AI faster than they can oversee it
By 2027, 60% of 5,000+ employee organizations will formalize AI governance
Fewer than 20% of such organizations have one today
Prediction draws on 1,200-leader survey and 400 conversations
Most enterprises run dozens to hundreds of AI use cases, often SaaS-sourced
Current AI oversight is mostly informal working groups
EU AI Act and state laws require documented assessments
41% of organizations reported an AI incident in 12 months
Nearly half of those could not identify accountability quickly
68% of boards requested AI risk reports, up from 29%
Client questions shifted to who is in charge of AI
Monthly working groups cannot keep pace with 200 models
Leading organizations will build governance as operating function
Laggards will build governance after incidents at higher cost
Name a single accountable executive for AI risk
Maintain a complete AI inventory including third-party AI
Tier AI use cases by risk
Give governance power to pause or block deployments
Track approval speed to avoid pushing teams to shadow AI

thesis: By 2027, 60% of large organizations will create funded, empowered AI governance functions as regulation, incidents and boards press.
